title: Polynomial residues exhaust the residue field when q vanishes
statement: Let K and F be fields, with a K-algebra structure on F. Let x ∈ F be transcendental over K, let q ∈ K[T] be irreducible, and let v : AlgebraicCurve.Place K F. Put A = v.toValuationSubring and let ρ : A → κ(v) be the canonical residue homomorphism. Assume every h ∈ A has an expression, in F, h = a(x)/b(x) with a,b ∈ K[T] and q not dividing b. Let e : K[T] → A be a K-algebra homomorphism whose composite with A → F is evaluation at x. If ρ(e(q)) = 0, then the ring homomorphism ρ ∘ e : K[T] → κ(v) is surjective.
lean_statement: ∀ (K F : Type*) [Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F] (x : F), Transcendental K x → ∀ q : Polynomial K, Irreducible q → ∀ v : AlgebraicCurve.Place K F, (∀ h : v.toValuationSubring, ∃ a b : Polynomial K, ¬ q ∣ b ∧ (h : F) = Polynomial.aeval x a / Polynomial.aeval x b) → ∀ e : Polynomial K →ₐ[K] v.toValuationSubring, (∀ a : Polynomial K, (e a : F) = Polynomial.aeval x a) → IsLocalRing.residue v.toValuationSubring (e q) = 0 → Function.Surjective ((IsLocalRing.residue v.toValuationSubring).comp e.toRingHom)
